nodes.summary: Let $e$ and $e'$ be injective maps $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with disjoint images, that is, $e(y) \ne e'(y')$ for all $y$ and $y'$. If the comparator lists $p$ and $q$ both have depth at most $d$, then $p$ with its wires relabeled by $e$, followed by $q$ with its wires relabeled by $e'$, has depth at most $d$.
nodes.title: Parallel composition of relabeled comparator lists

nodes.summary: For every $k$, the final layer of the odd-even merger on $2^{k+2}$ wires, which compares wires $2i + 1$ and $2i + 2$ for each $i < 2^{k+1} - 1$, has depth at most $1$: its comparators are disjoint.
nodes.title: The final layer of the odd-even merger has depth at most one

nodes.summary: For every $k$, Batcher's odd-even merger on $2^{k+1}$ wires has depth at most $k + 1$.
nodes.title: Depth bound for Batcher's odd-even merger

nodes.summary: For every $k$, there is a $d$ with $2d \le k(k+1)$ such that the comparator list of Batcher's odd-even merge sort on wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$ has depth at most $d$; that is, its depth is at most $k(k+1)/2$.
nodes.title: Depth bound for Batcher's odd-even merge sort as a comparator list

nodes.summary: If a comparator list has depth at most $d$ and $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is injective, then the comparator list obtained by relabeling its wires by $e$ also has depth at most $d$.
nodes.title: Relabeling wires preserves a depth bound

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the list of comparators $(2i + 1, 2i + 2)$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots, 2^{k+1} - 2$, in increasing order of $i$. It compares the neighbouring wires $2i + 1$ and $2i + 2$ and is the last layer of the odd-even merger on $2^{k+2}$ wires.
nodes.title: Last layer of the odd-even merger

nodes.summary: For all $k$ and $d$, if Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network on $2^k$ wires has depth at most $d$, then $k \le d$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the depth of Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, Batcher's odd-even merger on $2^{k+1}$ wires consists of exactly $k \cdot 2^k + 1$ comparators.
nodes.title: Size of the odd-even merger

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the number $L$ of comparators of Batcher's odd-even merge sort on $2^k$ wires satisfies $4(L + 1) + k \cdot 2^k = (k^2 + 4) \cdot 2^k$, that is, $L = (k^2 - k + 4) \cdot 2^k / 4 - 1$.
nodes.title: Size of Batcher's odd-even merge sort

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a comparator list and let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be injective. If two initial level assignments $\ell$ and $\ell'$ agree on every wire $e(y)$, then the levels after running $p$ with its wires relabeled by $e$, starting from $\ell$ and from $\ell'$, agree on every wire $e(y)$.
nodes.title: Levels of a relabeled comparator list on the image wires

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a comparator list, let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be any map and let $\ell$ be an initial level assignment. For every wire $x$ outside the image of $e$, the level of $x$ after running $p$ with its wires relabeled by $e$, starting from $\ell$, is $\ell(x)$.
nodes.title: Relabeled comparator lists leave the other wires alone

nodes.summary: Let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be injective, let $p$ be a comparator list and let $\ell$ be an initial level assignment. For every wire $j$, the level of wire $e(j)$ after running $p$ with its wires relabeled by $e$, starting from $\ell$, equals the level of wire $j$ after running $p$ starting from $\ell \circ e$.
nodes.title: Levels of a relabeled comparator list

nodes.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $f$ assign a Boolean value to each wire $0, 1, 2, \dots$, with false read as $0$ and true as $1$. Let $a, c \le 2^k$ be such that wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$ hold $a$ zeros followed by ones (wire $i < 2^k$ holds $0$ exactly when $i < a$) and wires $2^k, \dots, 2^{k+1} - 1$ hold $c$ zeros followed by ones (wire $2^k + i$, for $i < 2^k$, holds $0$ exactly when $i < c$). Then after…
nodes.title: The odd-even merger merges

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the odd-even merger on wires $0, \dots, 2^{k+1} - 1$ is the comparator list defined by recursion on $k$. For $k = 0$ it is the single comparator $(0, 1)$. For $k + 1$ it is the merger for $k$ with each wire $i$ renamed to $2i$ (merging the even wires), followed by the merger for $k$ with each wire $i$ renamed to $2i + 1$ (merging the odd wires), followed by the comparators $(2i + 1, 2i + 2)$…
nodes.title: Batcher's odd-even merger

nodes.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $f$ assign a Boolean value to each wire $0, 1, 2, \dots$, with false read as $0$ and true as $1$. After Batcher's odd-even merge sort on $2^k$ wires runs on $f$, there is $z \le 2^k$ such that every wire $j < 2^k$ holds $0$ exactly when $j < z$: wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$ hold $z$ zeros followed by ones.
nodes.title: Odd-even merge sort sorts every $0$-$1$ input

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, odd-even merge sort on wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$ is the comparator list defined by recursion on $k$. For $k = 0$ it is empty. For $k + 1$ it is the sorter for $k$ (sorting wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$), followed by the sorter for $k$ with each wire $i$ renamed to $2^k + i$ (sorting wires $2^k, \dots, 2^{k+1} - 1$), followed by Batcher's odd-even merger on $2^{k+1}$ wires.
nodes.title: Batcher's odd-even merge sort

nodes.summary: For every $k$, there is a $d$ with $2d \le k(k+1)$ such that Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network on $2^k$ wires has depth at most $d$; that is, its depth is at most $k(k+1)/2$.
nodes.title: Depth bound for Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every linearly ordered type $\alpha$, Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network on $2^k$ wires sorts every input over $\alpha$: for every assignment $v$ of elements of $\alpha$ to the wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$, the output of the network on $v$ is monotone in the wire order.
nodes.title: Batcher's odd-even merge sort sorts every input over every linear order

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the comparator network on the $2^k$ wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$ given by the comparators of Batcher's odd-even merge sort on $2^k$ wires, in the same order, with any comparator that touches a wire $\ge 2^k$ dropped.
nodes.title: Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network

nodes.summary: Let $ps$ be a list of comparators, each a pair of natural numbers, that lies within $[l, h)$, and let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $l' \le e(x) < h'$ for every $x$ with $l \le x < h$. Then the list obtained from $ps$ by relabeling its wires by $e$ lies within $[l', h')$.
nodes.title: Relabeling keeps comparators within an interval

nodes.summary: Given a map $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a list of comparators, each a pair $(i, j)$ of wires in $\mathbb{N}$, the relabeled list replaces every comparator $(i, j)$ by $(e(i), e(j))$ and keeps the order of the list.
nodes.title: Relabeling the wires of a comparator list

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ an assignment of values to the wires. Running the final layer for $k$ on $f$ gives at a wire $x$ the value $\min(f(x), f(x + 1))$ if $x$ is odd and $\lfloor x / 2 \rfloor < 2^{k+1} - 1$; otherwise the value $\max(f(x - 1), f(x))$ if $x$ is even, $x > 0$ and $(x - 2) / 2 < 2^{k+1} - 1$; and the value $f(x)$ in all other…
nodes.title: Output of the last layer of the odd-even merger

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ any map and $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ an assignment of values to the wires. For every list of comparators and every wire $x$ that is not of the form $e(y)$, running the list relabeled by $e$ on $f$ gives the value $f(x)$ at wire $x$.
nodes.title: Relabeled networks fix the wires outside the image

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be injective. For every list of comparators, every $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ and every wire $j$, running the list relabeled by $e$ on $f$ gives at wire $e(j)$ the same value as running the original list on the input $i \mapsto f(e(i))$ gives at wire $j$.
nodes.title: Running a relabeled network

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
